findings.title: Bound the finite-bath gas temperature solve by the gas thermodynamic domain
findings.trigger: A valid temperature-dependent mixture has positive Cv throughout its configured 100–3000 K domain, while a hot inert parcel has a separately valid 10000 K temperature. A dilute hot parcel leaves the correct gas equilibrium inside 100–3000 K.
findings.cause: Line 130 expands the gas-root bracket to parcel temperature. mixtureEnergy evaluates the gas polynomial outside its domain; positive Cv and monotonicity no longer hold there. The unverified 64-step sign bisection can converge to the wrong bracket endpoint. Subsequent reverse heat publication conserves zero exchange and returns success, hiding the missed physical transfer.
findings.proof: Reproduced by compiling the original production kernel as a serial CPU probe with full production primitive recovery and by launching the original CUDA kernel with a minimal state adapter using the production mixture caloric inversion. CUDA memcheck reports zero errors. Constant-Cp and in-range hot-particle controls pass. No production source was changed.
findings.requested_change: Use the existing gas thermo bounds/inversion policy for the gas-temperature root of E(T)+A*T. Retain actual parcel temperatures in B; do not clamp parcel inputs to the gas domain. Verify this valid in-domain root and retain source momentum/energy/species budgets.

shared_change_review: The branches have no textual file overlap, but pr26B changes common gas operators. The constant-viscosity active-mixture conductivity correction uses sum(Y*Cp(T)) instead of legacy bootstrap Cp and therefore can affect existing applications when that helper is active. It is a shared correctness change, not proof of complete behavioral independence. Pseudo-time traits remain inactive for original application layouts.
